title: Why Angkor Wat Faces the Wrong Way 🧭 #shorts
desc: Almost every temple at Angkor faces east, toward the sunrise. Angkor Wat faces west. Here's why historians think that is.

scenes.text: Why does Angkor Wat face the wrong way?
Almost all the temples around Angkor face east, toward the rising sun.
But Angkor Wat, the biggest of them all, faces west.
In Hindu tradition, the west is linked with the setting sun and with death.
So many historians think Angkor Wat was built as the tomb temple of its king, Suryavarman the Second.
And there's another surprise. On the spring equinox, the sun rises right over the central tower.
Facing west lets visitors at the entrance watch it happen. Follow Bolt for a new 'why' every day!
